note: Questions as an executive types them, each with 1-2 messy rephrasings (`messy`, asked as paraphrases) (short, messy, no use-case name). Each card names a family of evals/live_ops_keys.py, which picks the records it asks about and computes the key from the system of record on every run (scripts/eval_live_ops.py keys). A card asks about `instances` records; {slot} is the record's identifier. `facts` keeps only those facts of the family (default: all). Never an expected value here: keys are computed, stored outside the repository, and split dev / held out by evals.partition groups. Cards with "suite": "ceo" are the CEO suite (evals/live_ops_ceo.py and harder phrasings of core families): split on their own after the core (scripts/eval_live_ops.split), run alone with --suite ceo. Cards with "suite": "wide" (evals/live_ops_wide.py: answers in free text, harder shapes), "proactive" (the briefing's events), "roles" (run as the purchasing or quality reader too) and "open" (evals/live_ops_open.py: mined, blind and perturbed questions; a "perturb" card asks its base card's items with {"of", "ops"} applied to its words) are dealt per card after the CEO suite; the open suite's held-out half is reported as counts only. Cards with "suite": "inventory" (evals/live_ops_inventory.py) ask a CFO's reconciliation, costing and bill-and-hold questions, keyed from Sage invoice lines, FileMaker assembly orders and bills of materials.
